issues.problem: Pack contract-doc targets are not checked against other init targets. All steps preflight against the unchanged filesystem, so two steps can schedule incompatible writes to the same path.
issues.failure_scenario: A valid config declares the Expo pack and sets paths.backlog to docs/design-system.md. Both backlogStep and packDocsStep schedule that absent file; init writes the backlog and immediately overwrites it with the design-system template, then doctor reports a broken backlog that rerunning init cannot repair. Using that path for paths.closeouts instead can produce an EISDIR crash after earlier writes have already landed.
issues.suggested_fix: During preflight, reject duplicate and file/directory-overlapping write targets before applying anything, or validate pack-owned paths against configured state homes.
issues.evidence: steps.mjs:46-50 preflight maps every step against the unchanged tree. homes.mjs:24 (backlogStep) and packs.mjs:21-25 (packDocsStep) each schedule a WROTE row for an absent path. config.mjs:296 checks overlap only among paths.* keys, never against a pack manifest doc path (packs/expo/pack.mjs:93, docs/design-system.md). So paths.backlog set to docs/design-system.md gives two writes to the same file, and the later pack template overwrites the backlog. closeoutsStep (homes.mjs:38-46) schedules only '<closeouts>/.gitkeep', so a closeouts path equal to a pack doc path sees kind 'none', and the later writes to '<path>/.gitkeep' and to the file collide. The EISDIR crash is the plausible outcome of that collision, and I did not run it.

issues.problem: ruleProblem considers a pack doc-sync rule valid merely when its docs array contains the expected document. It does not verify the expected code pathspecs or reject additional alternative documents that weaken enforcement.
issues.failure_scenario: Configure expo:design-doc with docs: ["docs/design-system.md", "README.md"]. Doctor reports pack.expo.docs PASS, but a component change staged with only README.md satisfies the hook, so the design-system contract can drift. Likewise, changing code to src/screens/** leaves component changes entirely unchecked while doctor still passes.
issues.suggested_fix: Compare the configured pack-owned rule with the manifest's complete docSync definition: at minimum require all expected code pathspecs and exactly the expected docs list.
issues.evidence: The mechanism holds. packs.mjs:77 returns null whenever configured.docs.includes(doc.path), and it never compares configured.code with rule.docSync.code or rejects extra docs. docsync.mjs:34 accepts any one staged doc from rule.docs, so docs:['docs/design-system.md','README.md'] passes doctor yet is satisfied by staging README.md alone. A narrowed code list such as src/screens/** also passes doctor. Mitigations: plan.md:120 specifies the check only as the rule 'pointing at the doc', so the code matches the plan. The row can only WARN or PASS (disposition 11) and is advisory. Users may legitimately extend or retarget the rule. I could not show it breaks a stated requirement, so the severity is debatable and I did not confirm it.

issues.problem: dirents converts every readdirSync error into an empty directory, not just an absent or non-directory path.
issues.failure_scenario: If src/components or supabase/migrations exists but is unreadable due to permissions or an I/O error, doctor reports '0 primitives, 0 documented' or '0 migrations, 0 documented' as PASS, falsely claiming a successful measurement.
issues.suggested_fix: Return [] only for ENOENT and ENOTDIR; rethrow other errors so the doctor row reports that the check could not run.
issues.evidence: packages/cookwright/src/lib/packs/entries.mjs:21-26: dirents wraps readdirSync in a bare catch that returns [] for every error (EACCES, EIO), though its docblock says only absent or not-a-directory. listComponents (l.48) and listMigrations (l.60) then return empty lists, so an unreadable directory is indistinguishable from an empty one and reads as a measured 0.

issues.problem: uniqueItems does not enforce the runtime rule that each pack name appears once, because the schema permits two representations of a pack.
issues.failure_scenario: ["expo", {"name":"expo"}] is schema-valid since the two JSON values are distinct, but loadConfig refuses it with 'packs: each pack once'. Editors approve a configuration the CLI rejects.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a per-pack contains constraint with minContains 0 and maxContains 1 matching both representations, or normalize the schema to one representation.
issues.evidence: packages/cookwright/schema/cookwright.schema.json packs: uniqueItems:true with items oneOf [string enum, object {name,rules?}]. ['expo', {name:'expo'}] holds two distinct JSON values, so the schema accepts it. packages/cookwright/src/lib/config.mjs:244 collects names and pushes 'packs: each pack once' when the Set size differs. config.test.mjs:359 asserts the runtime rejects exactly this input. JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness by name across the two forms, so the gap is inherent and low severity, but the stated mismatch holds.

issues.problem: B-011's probe asks git about 'node_modules/' with a trailing slash. When node_modules is a symbolic link (some Docker, Nix or monorepo setups), `git check-ignore --no-index -- node_modules/` exits 128 ('pathspec is beyond a symbolic link'). probes.ignored throws on that, notIgnored turns it into a Refusal, and preflight refuses the whole init. Before this range, init worked in such a repo. The directory-only pattern `node_modules/` that init would append does not match a symlink either, so `git add -A` would still commit the link.
issues.suggested_fix: lstat `node_modules` first. If it is a symbolic link, probe and append `node_modules` without the slash; otherwise keep `node_modules/`. Or treat exit 128 on this one probe as 'not ignored' and append the slash-less line. Add an init test with node_modules as a symlink.
issues.failure_scenario: I ran this against HEAD: a scratch repo with `node_modules -> ../realnm` and no .gitignore. gitignoreStep({root}, {probes: PROBES}) throws `Refusal: git check-ignore node_modules/ failed: fatal: ... 'node_modules/' ... beyond a symbolic link`. `npx cookwright init` in that repo is refused outright, with no rows written, where the previous version succeeded.
issues.evidence: Reproduced in a scratch repo with `node_modules -> ../realnm`: `git check-ignore -q --no-index -- node_modules/` exits 128 ('beyond a symbolic link'), while the slashless form exits 1. packages/cookwright/src/lib/probes.mjs:62-68 throws on any status other than 0 or 1. gitignore.mjs:27 probes NODE_MODULES_LINE ('node_modules/', line 21) with that slash. The catch at lines 29-30 rethrows it as a Refusal. Before this range there was no node_modules probe. I did not run the full `npx cookwright init`; the refusal path follows from the code.

issues.problem: The primitive lister does not handle React Native platform extensions. `Map.web.tsx` and `Map.native.tsx` are listed as two primitives, `Map.web` and `Map.native`. A directory `Card/` holding only `index.ios.tsx` and `index.android.tsx` is not counted at all, because INDEX is /^index\.(tsx|jsx)$/. The template tells the user to key each row by 'file name without the extension'. A correctly documented `Map` row therefore leaves a WARN that never clears, and `Card` is never asked for.
issues.suggested_fix: Strip a platform suffix (.ios, .android, .native, .web) before naming a file primitive and dedupe. Accept `index.<platform>.(tsx|jsx)` as a directory index. Add both cases to entries.test.mjs.
issues.failure_scenario: I ran this against HEAD: listComponents(root, ['components']) over components/{Map.web.tsx, Map.native.tsx, Card/index.ios.tsx, Card/index.android.tsx} returns ['Map.native', 'Map.web']. With a design-system.md row `| Map | ... |`, pack.expo.docs reads WARN '2 of 2 primitives have no entry ...: Map.native, Map.web' indefinitely, and Card is missing from the count.
issues.evidence: entries.mjs:14-16,31-33: COMPONENT=/\.(tsx|jsx)$/ strips only the final extension, so Map.web.tsx and Map.native.tsx yield 'Map.web' and 'Map.native'. COMPANION (l.18) does not exclude platform suffixes. INDEX=/^index\.(tsx|jsx)$/ (l.15, used at l.40) rejects index.ios.tsx and index.android.tsx, so Card/ is not listed. A doc row keyed 'Map' therefore never matches either listed name.

issues.problem: For any ESLint config that is not Expo's template, init decides whether a pack is wired by a single-quoted substring, `require('cookwright/packs/<name>/eslint.cjs')`. It then tells the user to add `...require('…'),` by hand. In an `eslint.config.mjs`, `.ts` or `.mts` (ESM), `require` is undefined, so following that advice crashes ESLint with a ReferenceError. An ESM user who wires the pack correctly with `import expo from 'cookwright/packs/expo/eslint.cjs'`, or anyone using double quotes, is never recognised: the row reads 'skipped … add … by hand' on every run.
issues.suggested_fix: Match the export path itself (the module specifier in any quote style, via require or import). For a .mjs/.ts/.mts config, print an import-shaped line instead (`import expo from '…'; …expo`).
issues.failure_scenario: An Expo app whose eslint.config.mjs reads `import expoPack from "cookwright/packs/expo/eslint.cjs"; export default [...expoConfig, ...expoPack];`. Every `npx cookwright init` reports `skipped eslint.config.mjs … add ...require('cookwright/packs/expo/eslint.cjs') … by hand`. A user who instead pastes the advised require line into the .mjs file gets `ReferenceError: require is not defined` from `npx expo lint`.
issues.evidence: packs.mjs:60 detects wiring with text.includes(`require('${exportOf(mf)}')`), which is a single-quoted require only. An import of the pack, or a double-quoted require, is never matched. packs.mjs:62 then returns SKIPPED, so the row repeats on every run. The advised line comes from spreadLine (packs.mjs:44) and is a require() call, which is undefined in an ESM eslint.config.mjs, .mts or .ts. ESLINT_CONFIGS (packs.mjs:32) includes those extensions and the transform at packs.mjs:56 is limited to the CJS Expo template.

issues.problem: The pack's default doc-sync rule exempts only `*.test.*` files. The Jest and Expo convention of a `__tests__/` directory with `X-test.tsx` files and `__snapshots__/*.snap` is not exempt, so touching only a component test or a snapshot requires staging docs/design-system.md. The plan's ESLint ignores treat `**/__tests__/**` as test code, and the lister skips those directories, so the three measurements disagree on what a component is.
issues.suggested_fix: Add ':!**/__tests__/**' and ':!**/__snapshots__/**' to the expo pack's doc-sync code pathspecs (the docSync copy stays derived from the manifest), and add a doc-sync test with a `__tests__` file.
issues.failure_scenario: A fresh init on an app with `components/__tests__/ThemedText-test.tsx`. The developer updates that test's snapshot and commits only `components/__tests__/__snapshots__/ThemedText-test.tsx.snap`. Pre-commit doc-sync `expo:design-doc` refuses the commit until docs/design-system.md is staged, even though no component changed.
issues.evidence: packages/cookwright/packs/expo/pack.mjs:71 at 1355fc7 has code: ['src/components/**','components/**',':!**/*.test.*']. Only `*.test.*` is excluded. `components/__tests__/ThemedText-test.tsx` has no `.test.` segment, and `__snapshots__/*.snap` does not match it either. Both fall under `components/**`, so touching only them requires docs/design-system.md to be staged. docs/dev/bundles/stage-4/plan.md:124 ignores `**/__tests__/**` in the ESLint blocks, so the pack does treat `__tests__` as test code in one place and not in the doc-sync rule. I did not check the claim about the lister skipping those directories. The doc-sync mismatch holds without it.

It writes gate checks `npx cookwright standards --ratchet` and `--types`, but the CLI has no `standards` command yet (cli-main exits 2 on an unknown command, which is a gate fail; `skipExit` is validated but gate.mjs does not honour it until s5). Optionally, have the fixture run `npx expo lint` once (s4) and a pre-push or `bundle gate` (s5), so this class of dangling reference fails CI.

Then `npx expo lint` fails with `Cannot find module 'cookwright/packs/expo/eslint.cjs'`, and every `git push` fails at pre-push because `npx cookwright standards --ratchet` prints the usage and exits 2.
issues.evidence: Facts hold at 1355fc7: registry.mjs:34 RATCHET_CHECK 'npx cookwright standards --ratchet' (packDefaults :46); packs/ has only pack.mjs and templates (no eslint.cjs); eslintConfigStep exists at init/packs.mjs:70; cli-main.mjs:18-23 prints usage and exits 2 on an unknown command, and `standards` is not in it. gate.mjs is absent at that path.
